title: 0339-continuous-spacetime-video-superresolution-with-3d
universal_lens: Continuous space-time video super-resolution is formalized as a finite sum of local 3D sinusoidal basis functions. A Gaussian anti-aliasing kernel in frequency space modulates these bases, enabling principled, arbitrary-scale rendering without aliasing artifacts.
gsi_mapping: The Fourier field acts as a continuous latent prior over spatiotemporal coordinates. Bayesian inference treats the predicted amplitudes and phases as posterior parameters, while the Gaussian anti-aliasing term provides a conformal uncertainty bound on synthetic high-frequency details.
gse_mapping: Situational state transitions are modeled continuously rather than discretely. The VFF operator maps low-fidelity broadcast frames into a dense, differentiable phase-space representation, allowing GSE to query player kinematics at arbitrary sub-frame temporal resolutions.

primitives.verbatim_quote: The network predicts, for each local spatiotemporal patch, 512 sinusoidal basis functions with frequency ω_i, amplitude a_i, and phase φ_i.

primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when local motion exceeds the Nyquist limit of the highest predicted frequency or contains highly non-stationary, impulsive discontinuities.

primitives.name: Gaussian Frequency-Space Anti-Aliasing
primitives.verbatim_quote: A Gaussian anti-aliasing term ξ(ω_i, σ) scales each basis by a Gaussian in frequency space (i.e., spatial/temporal blur equivalent), enabling principled rendering at arbitrary scales without aliasing.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \omega_i: frequency magnitude (rad/pixel or rad/frame); \sigma: target blur width (pixels or frames); \xi: dimensionless scaling factor.
primitives.assumptions: The degradation process and desired upsampling scale can be accurately abstracted by an isotropic Gaussian blur in the frequency domain.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under severe real-world degradations like heavy H.264 compression blocking or directional motion blur, which violate the isotropic Gaussian assumption.

layer2.mapping: Functions as a GSI conformal prediction variance estimator, dynamically suppressing high-frequency hallucinations based on the requested output scale.
layer2.telemetry: Absence of Moiré patterns and high-frequency noise in upsampled outputs.

The core mathematical innovation of V3 lies in abandoning discrete grid reconstruction for a continuous implicit representation. By parameterizing a local video volume as a sum of 512 3D sinusoids, the model creates a differentiable mapping from continuous coordinates (x,y,t) to pixel intensities. This bypasses the rigid constraints of integer upsampling factors. However, simply evaluating a high-frequency Fourier series at finer grids induces severe aliasing. The authors introduce a Gaussian multiplier in the frequency domain, effectively acting as a low-pass filter whose cutoff is dynamically tied to the requested rendering scale. From a Foundry perspective, this dual structure—spectral expansion plus scale-dependent regularization—provides a rigorous framework for handling multi-scale visual data. The primary failure mode emerges from the 'synthetic-detail hazard.' Because the high-frequency components are statistically inferred rather than optically measured, they represent plausible hallucinations. In sports analytics, feeding these hallucinated edges into biomechanical tracking pipelines introduces catastrophic data-integrity risks. Therefore, the mathematical elegance of continuous reconstruction must be strictly quarantined from measurement-grade telemetry, serving only as a preprocessing enhancement for human review or robust detection front-ends.
